notes: Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-d67081, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by cc-442dc5. Verdict accept: no item, status, route or locator changed. This is the largest findings list this reviewer has handled — 160 recorded mistakes — and the review's main work was to test them against a text the extraction could not read. THE PUBLISHED VERSION IS AVAILABLE. The source block states that 'www.cambridge.org returned HTTP 404 or an HTML page instead of the PDF', so the journal's text was not read, its 160-page pagination is not used and every locator is to arXiv v5. That is retrievable after all: the landing page of doi:10.1017/fmp.2020.4 carries a citation_pdf_url meta tag with a very long, unguessable path, and that URL serves the PDF to a browser user-agent with a Cambridge referer. This review fetched it — 160 pages, matching the journal's stated pagination, printed page = PDF page — and recorded the retrieval recipe in the source block so the next worker need not rediscover it. The arXiv v5 hash the source block records was also re-fetched and matches byte for byte. ALL 160 FINDINGS WERE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE PUBLISHED TEXT so far as their quotations permit, and the verdicts say per finding which basis applies. 99 were located in the published article, so those slips are present in the work of record and not only in the preprint. 60 could not be located mechanically, because their quotations are mathematical displays that no text search reproduces from either PDF; for those the verdict says plainly that it rests on the extraction's reading of arXiv v5 and not on a check of this review's own. As calibration, six findings drawn from that group were spot-checked by targeted search — E2, E11, E40, E88, E120, E150 — and all six were found present in the published text, which is evidence about the group and is recorded as such rather than as a per-entry confirmation. ONE FINDING NEEDS ATTENTION, AND IT IS THE REASON THE PUBLISHED TEXT MATTERED. E160 is a bundle of about a dozen typographical slips, and at least three of them are NOT mistakes in the published work, because Cambridge's copyediting fixed them: v5's unbalanced '(upon restriction to U(V).' reads '(upon restriction to U (V )).' in print; v5's 'open neighborhood neighborhood U_v' reads 'open neighborhood U_v'; and v5's 'the isomorphisms 9' does not occur. Other elements of the same bundle do survive — 'For all w in Sigma and' and 'These sections, denoted' are present in both. Since the register records mistakes in PUBLISHED work, those three must be struck or the entry split. This review recorded the finding in E160's verdict rather than editing it, because re-partitioning a bundled entry is the extraction's call. The single library citation is correct: mathlib:AbstractMeasure at Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean:40 is 'def AbstractMeasure := C(X, R) →L[R] E', which is what the item claims for p-adic measures on a compact totally disconnected space. All 417 planned items name atlas layers that exist, all 40 missing items are routed exactly once, and there is no run-together numbering. Every check is listed in research/blueprint/reviews/REV-PAPER-EISCHEN-HARRIS-LI-ETAL-20.md.
